title: Rey and the Magic Branch
markdown:
The sun felt warm on Rey’s face, just like it did before he discovered the juiciest apples you ever did see. This one was like a big, warm wink, and the air smelled like a sweet, sugary dream. Rey’s nose twitched. Apples! Nana Tess’s apples were the juiciest, sunniest apples in the whole wide world. But today, a grumpy, grey frown of a problem stood in their way. The gate to the orchard was shut tight, jammed like a stubborn pebble.

"Hmph!" puffed Rey, pushing with his little hands. He pushed until his cheeks went pink. He pushed until his sneakers squeaked. The gate didn't budge. Not even a wiggle.

Saffron the parrot, her feathers a rainbow of sunshine and berries, bobbed on Rey’s shoulder. "Stuck! Stuck! Grumpy gate!" she squawked, giving the metal a little peck. It just made a loud CLANG.

Then, Nana Tess arrived, her basket swinging like a happy pendulum. "Oh my," she said, her voice as gentle as a summer breeze. "This old gate has a mind of its own today." She tried a firm push. Then she tried a strong pull. Still stuck tight. Rey’s shoulders drooped like wilting flowers. His tummy did a little flip-flop of frustration. He wanted apple-y goodness right now.

"It's no use," Rey sighed, his voice a little wobbly. "We'll never get our apple adventure." The prickly feeling of disappointment tickled his nose.

Just then, Nana Tess spotted a flurry of fallen leaves skittering near the gate. "Aha!" she declared. She picked up her long, bristly broom. Rey watched, his eyes wide. Nana Tess put the bristly end on the ground. Then, she pressed down on the other end, the handle end. WHOOSH! The leaves flew! "Look, Rey!" Nana Tess said, her eyes sparkling like dewdrops. "See how this end goes down, and that end goes up?"

Rey squinted. It was like a wobbly dance! The broom went down, and the leaves flew up! He scampered to the edge of the garden, where a long, fallen branch lay waiting. He grabbed a small, smooth stone. He wedged the end of the branch under the stone. Then, he pushed down on the other end of the branch. The stone lifted, just a tiny, tiny bit. "Whoa!" Rey gasped. Saffron ruffled her feathers, chirping, "Wow! Wow! Clever Rey!"

Rey looked around. He found another branch, this one much, much longer. He wedged the end of this long branch under the stone, too, right where he’d put the shorter one. Then, he pushed down on the free end. POP! The stone jumped up, higher this time! And guess what? It felt much, much easier! "It's easier with the long one!" Rey shouted, his voice full of surprise. "The longer the branch, the less I have to push!" A new feeling bubbled up inside him, not the wobbly frustration, but a fizzy, exciting buzz. This was like a super-duper puzzle!

"Nana Tess!" Rey yelled, running back as fast as his legs could carry him. "I know! I know how to open the gate!" He pointed to the longest, strongest branch he could find. With Saffron chirping a speedy song, "Lift! Lift! Smarty-pants Rey!" and Nana Tess helping him heave the big branch, they carefully positioned it under the heavy, stuck gate. They tucked one end of the branch underneath the gate, close to where it was stuck. The other end stuck out, long and ready.

"Okay," Rey whispered, taking a big, brave breath. "Here we go!" He pushed down with all his might on the far end of the branch. CREAK! The gate lifted. Just a little bit, but it lifted! "It's working!" Saffron shrieked, flapping her wings like a tiny aeroplane. Rey pushed again, a little harder. The gate creaked open a tiny bit more, making a gap just big enough.

"Hooray!" cheered Nana Tess, her smile as wide as the orchard. "We did it, explorers!"

Carefully, they wriggled through the little opening. The sweet, sun-warmed scent of apples filled their noses like a happy hug. Rey grinned, his tummy no longer doing flips of frustration, but feeling full and proud.

Back in the orchard, munching on a big, juicy apple that dripped sweet juice down his chin, Rey looked at the sturdy branch. "That branch," he said, his mouth full, "it was like a magic helper for lifting!"

Nana Tess smiled, wiping a smudge of apple juice from his cheek. "It is, in a way," she said kindly. "That's called a lever, Rey. When you push down on one end of a strong bar like this, it helps you lift something very heavy on the other end. It makes hard work much, much easier!"

Rey’s eyes popped open wide. "A lever! So that's why the long branch worked better!" He looked around the whole orchard. He saw the tall apple trees reaching for the sky. He saw the sturdy shed. He saw the winding path. "If levers can open gates, what else can they do?" He imagined using levers to build amazing things, to lift the biggest pumpkins, to help everyone in the village. The orchard suddenly felt like a treasure chest, full of even more wonderful secrets waiting to be found. "I wonder," he mused, taking another happy bite of his apple, "what other secrets are hiding in plain sight?"
characters: Rey the weather watcher, Saffron the parrot, Nana Tess
